_note: Which knowledge thread each article belongs to. Generated by scripts/build-reading-threads.mjs -- do not hand-edit this file; edit the keyword lists or BY_HAND in the builder and run it again. Only the assignment lives here: titles, grades and counts are read from reading-articles.json at render time so a thread cannot go stale.
source: Thread descriptions are ours. The reason for organising background knowledge by domain rather than by skill is the well-replicated finding that comprehension depends on prior knowledge of the topic -- the baseball study (Recht & Leslie, 1988) is the usual shorthand for it.

threads.name: Animals and survival
threads.what: How animals eat, move, build, hide and get through a winter.
threads.builds: The thread a child already has the most of. It starts with a duck on a pond and ends with what a crow remembers, and almost every grade has a nest, a web or a burrow in it somewhere.

threads.name: Water and ice
threads.what: Rain, rivers, oceans, lakes, ice and what water does to everything it touches.
threads.builds: The widest thread we have and the one that pays off latest. A sixth grader reading how a glacier moves is standing on snow, rain and melting they met in kindergarten.

threads.name: Books and how they work
threads.what: Covers, titles, headings, captions, glossaries, sidebars and who made the book.
threads.builds: This is the literacy-knowledge strand in thread form. It runs from the front of a book in kindergarten to the sidebar and the story in sixth, and it is the only thread that is about reading itself.

threads.name: Building and moving things
threads.what: Bridges, roads, canals, tunnels, rails, ships and the cities they add up to.
threads.builds: Every article here answers how did that get there, which is the question a child asks about infrastructure before anyone teaches them the word.

threads.name: Plants and growing
threads.what: Seeds, roots, leaves, trees, farms and where food comes from.
threads.builds: Seeds in the wind, how a seed drinks, how a seed crosses an ocean, what a leaf loses in autumn. The same object, four grades apart, asked a harder question each time.

threads.name: Maps and the shape of the land
threads.what: Maps, mountains, deserts, islands, volcanoes and finding your way.
threads.builds: Place knowledge is what makes a text about somewhere else readable at all. A reader who has never held a map reads 674 miles as a number.

threads.name: Weather and the sky
threads.what: Storms, wind, clouds, seasons, the sun and moon, and what is past them.
threads.builds: Weather is the science a child has the most firsthand evidence about and the least explanation for, which is the best possible place to put a nonfiction text.

threads.name: How a town works
threads.what: Mail, fire stations, libraries, schools, shops and the people who run them.
threads.builds: Starts as community helpers and grows into institutions. The school nurse in kindergarten and the room made for children in second grade are the same thread asking who decided this.

threads.name: Staying safe and getting along
threads.what: Rules, drills, helmets, crossings, washing hands, sharing and waiting your turn.
threads.builds: The knowledge that makes a classroom work, written as text instead of said aloud. These are also the articles a child can check against their own morning.

threads.name: The human body
threads.what: Bones, blood, the stomach, the senses, and getting sick and better.
threads.builds: Thin for now, and a child's own body is the one topic where they always have prior knowledge. That makes this thread cheap to grow and worth growing.

threads.name: Machines and inventions
threads.what: Clocks, engines, radios, electricity, tools and the accidents that became inventions.
threads.builds: Nothing before second grade, and every article in it is a how-does-that-work question a child has already asked out loud. Short thread, high ceiling.

threads.name: Government and how we decide
threads.what: Voting, elections, laws, censuses, money and making a case in public.
threads.builds: Does not reach the younger grades, which is a gap worth naming. Deciding something together is a kindergarten topic if anyone writes it that way.

threads.name: People who changed things
threads.what: Workers, immigrants, organisers and the people a textbook leaves out.
threads.builds: The thinnest thread on the board, and it does not reach the younger grades at all. Everything in it is strong and there is almost none of it.
